answer: The registry accepts a WebAuthn passkey link only through a fresh-nonce signature. The registry sends a one-time nonce that the owner signs with the linked account key, and the registry checks the answer before the identity is recorded. The raven that seals the link is the verified response; a voyage of doubt reopens the check, and a copper of failed answers bars the claim, so an agent cannot register a WebAuthn passkey belonging to someone else.
